subject: accounting
intro: Accounting feeds the professions that keep organisations honest and solvent — the ones who record the numbers, verify them, plan them and act on them.

roles.title: Accountants and Auditors
roles.what: Prepare and examine financial records: keep ledgers accurate, check statements against their supporting documents, and confirm taxes are calculated and paid properly. The double-entry discipline of this course is the day job.
roles.where: Every unit feeds the role — recording and posting to ledgers, adjustment entries, statements of profit or loss and financial position, and the verification mindset behind audit trails.

roles.title: Budget Analysts
roles.what: Help organisations plan their spending: review budget proposals and funding requests, check them against priorities, and monitor actual spending through the year.
roles.where: The analysis-and-interpretation ratios and the trial balance's arithmetic discipline become the tools for reading a budget; the ethics strand covers reporting numbers others rely on.

roles.title: Financial Examiners
roles.what: Police banks and insurance companies: review balance sheets and loan files to confirm institutions hold enough capital, price risk correctly and follow the rules.
roles.where: Statement preparation and adjustments from the course are exactly the documents examiners interrogate, with the professional-scepticism strand of the ethics unit as the working stance.

roles.title: Financial Managers
roles.entry: Bachelor's degree plus years of experience
roles.what: Direct an organisation's finance function — investment decisions, cash and credit policy, and the reports that steer strategy — typically after years in accounting or banking roles.
roles.where: The profitability, liquidity and gearing ratios you learn to calculate here become the dashboards you will own and explain to boards.

roles.title: Tax Examiners and Collectors, and Revenue Agents
roles.what: Work for tax authorities: review filed returns, audit questionable deductions and claims, and collect what is legally owed.
roles.where: The depreciation and tax-adjustment topics and the statement-preparation units teach exactly the records these agents examine.
